City Council Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

Request to Install White Curb at Willard Elementary School
The Traffic Commission received a request from the Superintendent of the Garvey School District, Anita Chu, on behalf of the Principal of Willard Elementary School, Michelle Collaso, to remove the green curb in front of the school and, instead, install a white curb for a loading and unloading zone.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council approve the Traffic Commissionâ€™s recommendation to remove the green curb in front of Willard Elementary School and, instead, install approximately 50-feet of white curb for a loading and unloading zone.
Staff Report
C.
Request to Install Red Curb â€“ 5012 Walnut Grove Avenue
The Traffic Commission received a request from Talal Trabolsi of Jacobs Engineering Group, the lead construction management company for the Alameda Corridor Extension (ACE) Trench Project for the Walnut Grove Avenue Crossing, for the extension of the existing 20-feet red curb at 5012 Walnut Grove Avenue all the way to the rail road crossing, which is approximately 100 additional feet. According to Mr. Trabolsiâ€™s request, this is needed due to the installation of new striping as part of the ACE Trench Project, which will no longer accommodate parking in this area.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council approve the Traffic Commissionâ€™s recommendation to extend the existing 20-feet of red curbing at 5012 Walnut Grove Avenue to the rail road crossing, approximately 100 additional feet.
Staff Report
D.
Resolution 2018-03 â€“ Providing Permission to Councilmember Alarcon to be Absent from Council Meetings Pursuant to Government Code Section 36513
At their October 24, 2017, meeting, the City Council approved Resolution 2017-59, providing permission to Councilmember Alarcon to be absent from Council meetings pursuant to Government Code Section 36513 until December 12, 2017, to attend to a personal health issue.
California Government Code Section 36513 provides that the City Council may grant permission to a Councilmember to be absent from Council meetings for a period longer than 60 days, which if unexcused, would result in their office becoming vacant.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council has the following options:
1.
Adopt Resolution 2018-03, providing permission for Councilmember Alarcon to be absent from Council meetings up to an including February 27th pursuant to Government Code Section 36513; or A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROSEMEAD, CALIFORNIA, GRANTING PERMISSION TO COUNCILMEMBER ALARCON TO BE ABSENT FROM COUNCIL MEETINGS PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE 36513
2.
Another option presented by the City Council.

The City Council will consider authorizing the attendance of any Council Member who wishes to attend the National League of Cities 2018 Congressional City Conference in Washington, on March 11 â€“ 14, 2018.
If majority of the City Council wishes to attend the Conference and will not be present for the regular City Council Meeting scheduled on March 13, 2018, then the March 13, 2018, meeting will be cancelled due to a lack of quorum.
In addition, if a majority of Council attends the conference and the majority wishes to meet with a legislative body to discuss issues of general interest to the public, a special meeting agenda will be posted.

A.
Traffic Signal Maintenance and Repair Agreement and Budget Amount Increase â€“ St. Francis Electric
On December 12, 2017, staff requested that the City Council increase the annual contractual amount for St. Francis Electric as a result of needed repairs and necessary equipment upgrades, which were not accurately budgeted under the original contract (see Attachment A). Due to a lack of supporting documentation to the staff report, the City Council requested that this item be brought back to their meeting of January 9, 2018.
St. Francis Electric is currently under a two-year contract that began January 30, 2017, with an option to renew for two additional years, to monitor all of the City-owned traffic signals, flashing beacons, in-pavement flashing crosswalks, and electronic speed feedback signs at a flat monthly fee of $4,456.25 or $53,475 annually. In addition, the contract includes a variety of costs as related to the maintenance and/or repair of worn-out, damaged, or faulty equipment (see Attachment B). As a result, an additional $53,475 was budgeted to cover these costs in the Cityâ€™s budget under the Traffic Signal Maintenance Services account.
Recommendation: It is recommended that Council approve an amendment to the contract with St. Francis Electric to include a â€œnot to exceedâ€ maintenance amount of $71,800 for St. Francis Electric in addition to the already approved $53,475 monitoring amount and authorize the City Manager to execute the amended contract.

At the Council meeting of December 12th, the City Council voted to offer the position of City Manager to Gloria Molleda. Since that time the City Attorney and Ms. Molleda have come to an agreement on terms for a contract for the Council to consider, which are the same terms that were included for the prior City Manager.
Recommendation: The City Council approve a contract with Gloria Molleda for the position of City Manager.
